title: IllusionGameEEG_data
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalography, physiological, and behavioral data collected from 103 healthy individuals (ages 21-45) during visual illusion perception tasks and resting-state recordings. Participants performed perceptual judgments on three classic visual illusions (Ebbinghaus, Müller-Lyer, and Vertical-Horizontal) with manipulated difficulty and illusion strength, followed by an 8-minute eyes-closed resting-state period. The multimodal dataset includes 64-channel EEG, electrocardiogram, photoplethysmography, and respiration signals, enabling investigation of neural correlates of visual illusion sensitivity and resting-state brain activity.
methods_description: EEG signals were recorded using a 64-channel EasyCap with BrainVision Recording system at 10,000 Hz sampling rate, with electrodes placed according to the 10-5 system and impedance maintained below 12 kOhm. Physiological signals (ECG, PPG, and respiration) were acquired at 1,000 Hz using PLUX OpenSignals software and BITalino Toolkit. ECG was recorded using modified Lead II configuration, respiration via abdominal belt, and PPG via finger clip on the non-dominant hand.
